AsyncQualifierLiveRaceStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a synchronous racetime qualifier race (PR 10).

``(str, Enum)`` (not ``StrEnum``) — render ``.value`` in f-strings, never the
bare member (which repr's as ``AsyncQualifierLiveRaceStatus.FINISHED``).

``SCHEDULED`` before a room opens, ``PENDING`` once a room exists but the race
has not started, ``IN_PROGRESS`` while racing, ``FINISHED`` once the entrants'
results are captured into runs, ``CANCELLED`` when the racetime room was
cancelled instead of raced.

``CANCELLED`` exists because the inbound handler used to update only the
``RacetimeRoom`` on a cancellation, leaving the race stuck at scheduled or
in-progress and indistinguishable from one still to come.
AsyncQualifierLiveRaceStatus.title: AsyncQualifierLiveRaceStatus

BracketState.description:
Lifecycle of a bracket stage.

``DRAFT`` while entrants are enrolled/seeded (the engine has not run yet);
``ACTIVE`` once ``start`` generates and persists the match graph;
``COMPLETE`` once every match is resolved and ``final_rank`` is written.
``CANCELLED`` is the close-out for a stage that was started and then
abandoned — without it the only way to finish such a stage is to fabricate a
winner for every remaining match. It is terminal like ``COMPLETE`` but writes
no ``final_rank``, so nothing downstream can draw a field from it.
BracketState.title: BracketState

MyQualifierRunResponse.description:
One of the caller's own runs — a narrower projection than the admin view.

Separate from :class:`AsyncQualifierRunResponse` because the two audiences are
not the same. An exact ``score`` is exactly solvable for the seed's par (the
caller knows their own ``elapsed_seconds``), so it is withheld while the
qualifier is open and ``score_band`` stands in; a reviewer reading
``/{id}/runs`` still gets the number. The projection also carries what the
runner needs and the model alone did not spell out: the seed played, the
deadline an in-progress run dies at, and whether a void was a reviewer's.

info.description:
Scripts, bots and spreadsheets can do through this API what people do in the
Wizzrobe web app: read the schedule, sign up for crew, run matches, record
results, and manage a community's setup.

## Getting a token

Open your home page, go to the **Profile** tab and expand **API tokens & AI
clients**, then choose **Generate token**. The token is shown once, so copy it
straight away. Send it on every request:

    Authorization: Bearer wizzrobe_pat_xxxxxxxx...

Click **Authorize** above and paste it to try endpoints from this page.

- **A token belongs to one community.** You pick the community when you make
  it, and every call works inside that community only. To work with two
  communities, make two tokens.
- **A token acts as you.** It can do exactly what you can do in the web app,
  no more. Each endpoint says who can call it.
- **Read-only tokens** can call `GET` endpoints only. Anything that changes
  data answers `403`.
- Tokens can expire, and you can revoke one at any time from the same card.

A personal token is for your own scripts. An app someone else wrote signs you
in with OAuth instead, and gets only the **scopes** you approve. Each endpoint
lists the scope an app needs to call it; a few say apps can't call them at all.

## Conventions

- **Times are UTC**, in ISO 8601 (`2026-10-16T18:00:00Z`). Convert to local
  time before showing them to people. Reports are the exception: their times
  are on the community's own clock, with the UTC offset included.
- **Errors** come back as JSON with a `detail` message:
  `{"detail": "Staff access required"}`. `400` means a rule refused the
  request (the message says which), `401` a missing or expired token, `403` no
  permission, a read-only token or a scope the app wasn't given, `404` nothing with that id in your
  community or a feature your community hasn't turned on, `422` a malformed
  request.
- **Rate limit:** 120 requests a minute per token, and the same
  across everything coming from one network address. Over that you get `429`
  with a `Retry-After` header giving the seconds to wait.
- Some sections only work when the community has turned the feature on
  (Admin → Features). Those endpoints say so.
- **Events.** A community runs events (one weekend each). Event-day
  endpoints work in the community's default event unless you add
  `?event=<slug>`; `GET /api/events` lists the slugs. A call about one row (a
  match, a shift) works in that row's event whatever you pass, and naming a
  different event answers `404`. An archived event is read-only: writes to it
  answer `409`.

## Recipes

Set two shell variables first. `WIZZROBE` is the address you open Wizzrobe at.

    export WIZZROBE=https://onsite.speedgaming.org
    export TOKEN=wizzrobe_pat_xxxxxxxx...

**Check your token works**, and see who it acts as:

    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$WIZZROBE/api/users/me"

**Today's matches on one stage.** Find the stage id with `GET /api/stages`,
then filter by it and a time window (UTC):

    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
      "$WIZZROBE/api/matches?stage_id=3&start_date=2026-10-16T00:00:00Z&end_date=2026-10-17T00:00:00Z"

**Sign up to commentate a match.** A crew coordinator still has to approve you:

    curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"role": "commentator"}' "$WIZZROBE/api/matches/812/crew"

**Record the winner of a match.** `winner_id` is the `id` of the winning entry
in the match's `players` list, not the person's user id:

    curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"winner_id": 1534}' "$WIZZROBE/api/matches/812/result"

**Receive events instead of polling.** Staff can point a webhook at your
server (Admin → Settings → Integrations → Webhooks). What it sends, and how to
check the signature, is under **Webhooks** at the bottom of this page.

post.description:
Sent to a webhook subscribed to any of these events, or to `*`:

- `async_qualifier.closed`
- `async_qualifier.live_race_recorded`
- `async_qualifier.opened`
- `async_qualifier.run_expired`
- `async_qualifier.run_forfeited`
- `async_qualifier.run_reattempted`
- `async_qualifier.run_reviewed`
- `async_qualifier.run_submitted`

Answer with any `2xx` within 10 seconds. Anything else is retried, up to 3 attempts in all, waiting longer each time. Redirects are not followed.

Check the signature against the raw body bytes before trusting a delivery:

    import hmac, hashlib
    signed = f"{headers['X-Wizzrobe-Timestamp']}.{raw_body}".encode()
    expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret.encode(), signed, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    assert hmac.compare_digest(expected, headers["X-Wizzrobe-Signature"])

Reject deliveries whose timestamp is more than a few minutes old.
